D.t: Cory Booker leads by 25.6 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 915,854 votes; a one point swing is about 17,860 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +16.6 and D +35.1. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Essex, a projected net 174,662 votes; Hudson, a projected net 107,205 votes; Middlesex, a projected net 102,734 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Monmouth, D +12.0, 8.0% of the vote; Gloucester, D +8.9, 3.7% of the vote; Sussex, R +7.6, 1.8% of the vote; Hunterdon, D +11.2, 1.8% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Cory Booker runs furthest behind in Burlington, Mercer, Gloucester. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 69% of voters, 55 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.43 points; Voters without a degree, 51% of voters, 60 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.54 points; Men, 47% of voters, 56 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.34 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Cory Booker: Immigration voters 32 to 65, Midsize counties 51 to 45, White voters 55 to 42. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
